back: IAS 32 (presentation: debt vs equity) · IFRS 9 (recognition & measurement) · IFRS 7 (disclosures) · IFRS 13 (fair value) · IFRS 2 (share-based payment).

Contractual obligation to deliver cash (interest/repayment) that the issuer cannot avoid → liability. Otherwise equity (residual). "If you have to write a cheque, it can't be equity." Label and probability irrelevant.
Holder can require redemption (put) → liability. Issuer has the option to redeem (call) → equity.
Conditions outside the issuer's control (reference rates, CO2 targets) do not make an instrument equity. Payments linked to discretionary dividends on ordinary shares → equity.
Liability: interest expense in P/L; issue costs deducted from the liability and spread via the effective interest rate. Equity: dividends in equity; issue costs deducted from equity.
Mix of debt and equity features (subordination, very long or perpetual maturity, deferrable interest). Classified as a whole by the obligation criterion – often equity if interest can be deferred.
Convertible bonds, bonds with warrants: split accounting – liability = PV at market rate, equity = remainder (e.g. 100 → 95 debt + 5 equity). No intermediate category in IFRS.
Share capital (par) · share premium/APIC · retained earnings · accumulated OCI · less treasury shares.
Outstanding (held externally) ≤ issued (incl. treasury shares) ≤ authorised (board may issue).
Cash = number × issue price; share capital = number × par; share premium = rest; issue costs reduce share premium.
Buy-back: treasury shares (negative equity) at cost. Resale: cash in, treasury released at cost, difference to share premium – never P/L. Cancellation: share capital −par, share premium −rest.
Initial: issue price (net of costs). Interest expense = effective rate × opening carrying amount; cash = coupon × nominal; difference amortises discount/premium.
